newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile closes coal mine, defying union protests.
newsitem.headline: Chile closes coal mine, defying union protests.

text.p: The Chilean government closed Wednesday a state-owned coal mine in the southern town of Lota, defying miners' unions that had struggled for years to keep the pit open despite constant deficits.

The century-old Lota mine officially shut its gates for good at 3 p.m.(2000 GMT) after the government surprised workers early in the day by announcing it would be closed and that any protests against the move were futile.
''The government has made a decision that is absolutely irrevocable,'' said Interior Minister Carlos Figueroa.

The government later announced a two-year $44 million ''development plan'' for the depressed Lota area, one of the worst pockets of poverty in booming Chile, and said that two other state-owned coal mines and a processing plant will stay open.

The mine belongs to state coal company Enacar, which survives thanks only to heavy state subsidies. Lota was the scene of a bitter, two-month strike last year by workers protesting ''modernization'' plans including the laying off of about 100 workers.

Employing about 1,100 people, the mine became of symbol of resistance by unions and their left-wing supporters to President Eduardo Frei's free-market economic policies. To Enacar's critics, Lota was a symbol of government waste and misguided paternalism.
Enacar, which also operates the Trongol mine in the town of Curanilahue and the Carbonifera Victoria mine in the town of Lebu, posted a $46 million loss last year.
